name: Primary Inferior Vena Cava Aneurysm

criteria.description: Focal aneurysmal dilation of the inferior vena cava confirmed by imaging
Exclusion of secondary causes such as trauma, infection, or neoplasm
Presence of symptoms related to venous obstruction or thrombosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal aneurysmal dilation of the inferior vena cava on imaging with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging and clinical exclusion of other causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Rarely palpable but highly indicative when present

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inferior vena cava aneurysmal dilation on imaging
searchTerms: bulging of inferior vena cava on scan

common.symptomName: Venous thrombosis symptoms (e.g., leg pain, swelling)
common.notes: Due to turbulent flow within aneurysm
searchTerms: leg pain and swelling from blood clots

occasional.symptomName: Deep vein thrombosis in lower limbs
searchTerms: blood clots in deep leg veins

rare.symptomName: Rupture of inferior vena cava aneurysm
searchTerms: rupture of large abdominal vein aneurysm
bursting of inferior vena cava aneurysm

rare.symptomName: Compression of adjacent structures causing hydronephrosis
searchTerms: swelling of kidney due to vein compression

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to venous return alteration
searchTerms: irregular heartbeats from vein blood flow changes
arrhythmias due to altered venous return
heart rhythm problems from vein issues

laboratory: D-dimer elevation in cases with thrombosis
Normal inflammatory markers unless secondary complications
imaging: CT or MRI demonstrating focal aneurysmal dilation of the inferior vena cava
Ultrasound Doppler showing turbulent venous flow
genetic: No known genetic mutations identified; primarily sporadic
other: Histopathology (if surgical specimen) showing venous wall thinning without inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, infection, or neoplasm
Predominant thrombus without venous wall dilation

redFlags: Sudden onset abdominal pain indicating possible aneurysm rupture
Signs of pulmonary embolism such as sudden dyspnea or chest pain
Rapidly increasing abdominal mass or venous distension
